title: Method barrier for translation-annihilator interpolation bounds (L2) and CM deficit family (L3)
question: L2 (method barrier): for any translation annihilator D = Σ_{i∈S} c_i G(Q+iP) with Σc_i = Σ i c_i = 0 (|S| = s, width w), G = g∘x, deg g = d >= 1, 2N < r: D ≢ 0 has pole degree exactly 2ds and >= 2(N − w) zeros, so N <= ds + w, minimized at s = 3, w = 2 (Theorem C). Hence zero-counting with translates cannot beat N/3; a tighter bound requires information beyond pole structure and values G(kP) = f(k). L3: on anomalous j = 0 curves (p ≡ 1 mod 3, #E = p), the interpolant of k^2 at N = (p−1)/2 satisfies g(ζX) = λ^2 g(X), so g = X^s h(X^3) and deg g <= N − 3 + s.
rationale: From ECDLP-33; answers whether Theorem C's 1/3 can be improved by the same technique (no).
